scenes.text: NASA's seismometer on Mars felt the planet shake more than thirteen hundred times.
The InSight lander touched down on November twenty sixth, twenty eighteen.
It hit the Martian atmosphere at about twelve thousand three hundred miles per hour.
Then a parachute and rocket engines slowed it to about five miles per hour.
Engineers call this part the seven minutes of terror.
InSight landed on a flat lava plain called Elysium Planitia, near the equator.
Its French built seismometer detected its first marsquake in April twenty nineteen.
In May twenty twenty two, it caught the biggest one, estimated at around magnitude five.
Those quake waves showed that the center of Mars is molten.
They also showed its core is about half the size of Earth's core.
But its heat probe, nicknamed the mole, got stuck less than half a meter underground.
Dust slowly covered its solar panels, and the mission ended in December twenty twenty two.
By then, it had worked on Mars for more than four years.
What do you want the next Mars lander to discover?

title: NASA felt Mars shake over 1,300 times 🫨
caption: NASA's InSight landed on Mars on Nov 26, 2018 and recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes. Its data showed the center of Mars is molten.
